images.title: What an *AI Executive Assistant* does, and what it costs
images.sub: Inbox, calendar, travel and meeting prep, split into what an AI Employee owns and what stays with the person it works for.

images.name: duties
images.title: The assistant job, *duty by duty*
rows: Sorts everything overnight, answers routine requests and puts the emails that need the owner on one list with a draft under each.
Offers times, sends invites, moves meetings when someone cancels and follows the owner's scheduling rules.
Books and rebooks within a written policy and keeps one itinerary on the calendar. Anything outside policy goes to the owner.
Writes a one-page brief before each meeting and drafts the follow-up and action items after it.
Files receipts, sends contracts for signature and puts renewals and deadlines on the calendar.
Drafts the reply. The owner agrees to anything new and approves money above the limit.

images.name: day-on-shift
images.title: A day for a *law firm partner*
rows: Sorts 112 overnight emails. Eight need the partner and go on one list, each with a drafted reply.
A client asks to move Thursday's call. It offers two open times and sends the new invite.
A prospective client wants to sign an engagement letter. It drafts a reply and holds it for the partner.
Wednesday's flight is cancelled. It rebooks within policy and moves the dinner reservation.
An unhappy client emails about a bill. It drafts nothing and sends it straight to the partner.
Writes the brief for tomorrow's client meeting: matter status, last bill, last three emails.
Someone asks about a transfer from the trust account. It confirms nothing and asks the partner.

images.name: setup
images.title: How an AI Executive Assistant *is set up*
steps: Who always gets through, which hours stay clear, the travel policy, and what the owner never says in writing.
Delegate access to email and calendar, plus the drive, the CRM and travel accounts, with only the access the job needs.
What it sends and books alone, and what waits: new commitments, money above a limit, confidential matters.
It writes every reply and the owner presses send. Each edit teaches it tone and priorities.
Hand over one category at a time
Scheduling confirmations first, then document requests, as the drafts stop needing changes.
Someone reads the log and updates the rules when people, policies or tools change.
